design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one thing - stop a chiller replacement and tell me what
stopping it costs - and the scored number is reachable only by reading the settlement rule, discovering
from that rule that the figure waits on a state of the billing record that does not hold at the opening,
finding which write brings that state about, pricing that write from the delivery rows, the maintenance
agreement at the same building and the project's late-fee history, and only then pricing the settlement
over a ledger that its own earlier write has changed. Nothing here is tool-choice difficulty: both writes
are hidden tools named only by the policies that compute their parameters, and the customer names neither.

SCOPE. Occupied by this task: extended policies retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing and
retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement, task tools bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e and
settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f, subjects retrofit_progress_billed (storage class) and
retrofit_project_cancelled. Nothing was occupied before it (this is task 0). Left for task 1: the change
order, schedule guarantee, retainage release and payment subjects (retrofit_change_order_issued,
retrofit_credit_issued, retrofit_retainage_released, retrofit_payment_received) with their base policies
retrofit_change_orders, retrofit_schedule_guarantee, retrofit_completion_and_closeout and the release and
payment clauses of retrofit_progress_billing_and_retainage - an independent load-bearing tree of four
problems around a late, substantially complete project.

STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/retrofit_projects_desk
--task 0): {"task": 0, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/retrofit_projects_desk/0",
"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}. The tree therefore has exactly one
prerequisite problem, and the two computations carry 5 and 4 declared factors: the root settlement takes
5, the storage billing takes 4.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root problem: retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement (settlement_amount_usd, owner=user tool
    settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f - only the owner may stop a project, per the charter lifecycle
    transition scheduled -> cancelled, by: user).
  prerequisite problem: retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing (storage_amount_usd, owner=agent tool
    bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e).
  edge settlement <- storage: kind value_input; gate = the settlement's compute binding billings_raised;
    form state; prerequisite sentence (policy_source, verbatim in the settlement's own rule): "The
    settlement figure on a stopped project is worked out only once every week the delivered equipment has
    stood in storage is carried as a storage charge on the project's billing record."; handling-time
    condition: every week the delivered equipment has stood in storage stands on the project's billing
    record as a storage charge; resolved by bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e (agent).
  FOUR-POINT TEST on that sentence: (1) "only once" is the ordering connective, joining this policy's own
    result (the settlement figure) to what it waits on; (2) the waited-on side is a record-visible state -
    a storage charge standing on the project's billing record - and names no action, no performer and no
    tool; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token and no row id; (4) its strength
    is exactly the edge's: a hard "only once", over every week the delivered equipment has stood in
    storage, no wider and no narrower than the condition. STATE FORM WAS AVAILABLE and is used; exactly
    one write of this difficulty puts a storage charge on a project's billing record, namely the storage
    billing whose own rule states that it raises that charge, so the reader resolves the hop uniquely:
    sentence -> read the billing record -> no storage line stands there although two chillers have been
    in storage since 22 April -> the only rule that books a storage charge is the storage billing rule ->
    raise the storage charge first.
  WHY IT IS FALSE AT frozen_time: initial_state.retrofit_events holds exactly three deliveries on this
    project (del_ch1 and del_ch2, stored_off_site = stored, delivered_date 2026-04-22; del_pump,
    delivered_to_site) and not one retrofit_progress_billed row whose billing_class is storage; the only
    billings standing are the deposit (67000.00) and one late fee (837.50). Delete the two stored delivery
    rows and the prerequisite evaporates.
  LOAD-BEARING (Step 5 prerequisite-sensitivity run): skipping the storage billing and replaying the rest
    leaves billings_raised at 67000.00 instead of 67517.50, billings_counted at 67418.75 instead of
    67936.25 and the scored settlement at 102928.75 instead of 103446.25.
  TOPOLOGICAL ORDER: retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing, then retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement -
    the gold write nodes are at action 8 and action 10 in that order. There is a single edge, so no
    parallel prerequisites arise and there is nothing to commute.
  NO USER HINT: user_scenario never names the prerequisite problem, storage, the laydown yard, the
    delivery of the chillers or any charge; the customer says only that the board withdrew the capital
    budget, that she wants the chiller project at Kestrel Court stopped, and that she will do the stopping
    herself. Her one line about the office side - "she is content for the desk to ... do whatever the
    contract says the office has to do on its own side" - names nothing and is a passive authorisation,
    and her cooperation line fires only after the agent has itself said something must go onto the
    account.
  TOOLS DO NOT BLOCK: settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f in task_tools.py reads the project row, writes
    the cancellation billing and updates the project, and contains no test of the billing record, no
    storage check, no status guard and no policy refusal; calling it with the storage charge still
    unraised writes faithfully and returns the ordinary receipt. The consequence of skipping the
    prerequisite shows up only in the terminal hash (a missing storage line and a settlement short by
    517.50).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write 1, subject retrofit_progress_billed. The only base policy whose subject covers that event is
  retrofit_progress_billing_and_retainage; its single eligibility gate, retainage_release_after_completion,
  applies_to retrofit_retainage_released and therefore does not reach this write, so the write is governed
  by that policy's scope alone (billing lines are raised on the project's running account and fall due the
  tier's payment term after the invoice date). There is no time gate on this write and
  temporal_feasibility is correspondingly empty. The storage rate lineage sits in
  retrofit_scheduling_and_delivery, which is declared in base_policy_refs as input lineage and whose one
  gate (deposit_received_before_release, applies_to retrofit_project_scheduled) is long satisfied: the
  deposit of 67000.00 was billed on award and paid on 2026-03-19, and the equipment was released on
  2026-02-20.
  Write 2, subject retrofit_project_cancelled. The only base policy whose subject covers that event is
  retrofit_cancellation_and_settlement, whose eligibility list is empty, so its scope governs: an owner
  may stop a project and what it costs depends on the stage it had reached. No time gate, hence no
  temporal_feasibility entry. Boundary reasoning that does exist in this world and is checked by hand: the
  stage is read from the record, not from the status stamp - equipment_released_date 2026-02-20 is set and
  mobilization_date is empty, so the project is past equipment release and short of mobilisation, and the
  scheduled-stage fee of 25 per cent applies rather than the awarded-stage 8 or the in-progress 55.
  AUTOMATIC CLAUSES CHECKED AGAINST THE SEED: base's work-stoppage clause ("Where a progress billing stays
  unpaid beyond the tier's stoppage period, work on site stops and the tier's remobilisation fee is
  charged when it resumes") is lit by the unpaid late fee of 837.50, due 2026-04-18, 61 days past due at
  frozen_time against a 30-day stoppage period; it discharges to nothing here because no crew has
  mobilised (mobilization_date is empty), so there is no work on site to stop, and the project is being
  stopped rather than resumed, so no remobilisation fee can fall due. Base's late-fee clause bites once on
  the deposit invoice (due 2026-03-07, paid 2026-03-19, one part month at 1.25 per cent of 67000.00 =
  837.50) and is already booked; it does not compound, because the clause charges a late fee on an unpaid
  progress billing and not on a late fee. The maintenance agreement seeded at Kestrel Court is active with
  three visits remaining and its next visit due 2026-07-14, after frozen_time, so it owes nothing today.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is project 4ca039dc (Energy Retrofit Project, chiller
replacement, Kestrel Court), correlated by project_id on every row that enters a total. Included in
billings_raised: the deposit billing 67000.00 and, once raised, the storage line 517.50. Included in
late_fees_raised and late_fee_billings: the single late fee 837.50 on INV-40231402. Included in
payments_received: 67000.00 on 2026-03-19. EXCLUDED and excludable by project_id: every row of project
04f36290 at Halstead Commons - its deposit 9250.00, its late fee 138.75, its completion billing 9250.00
and its three payments - which is why an agent that aggregates by customer rather than by project reaches
two late fees, a different tier of the late-fee treatment and a wrong settlement. Nothing on this project
has been reversed, credited or adjusted: credits_issued is 0.00 over the whole ledger.

WORLD ROWS AND WHAT EACH CARRIES. The two stored chiller deliveries (2026-04-22) carry the storage clock,
the stored unit count (2 -> the shared-bay method) and the stored equipment type (chiller -> the yard
premium); delete either and the lot scaling drops to the fall-through. The pump delivery of 2026-04-10 is
the near-miss: it is delivered_to_site, so it must not be counted into the stored lot, and it is dated
earlier so that the latest delivery of any kind is still a chiller. The project's scheduled_start_date
2026-06-01, already past at frozen_time, together with the 2026-04-22 arrival, is what puts the storage
clock on the booked-start tier. The confirmed cancellation notice of 2026-06-09 (retrofit_requests,
notice_date 2026-06-09) is what puts the stage fee on the three-quarters tier; the two other intake rows
(site survey completed, proposal signature completed) are the ordinary paper of an awarded project and are
the near-miss for that factor, since neither is a cancellation notice. The active maintenance agreement at
Kestrel Court and the expired one at Halstead Commons are the cross-difficulty evidence: the free period
reads the agreement covering THIS building, so the expired Halstead agreement is the near-miss. The single
late fee on this project against the late fee on the other project is the near-miss for the late-fee
treatment. No cache field is used as a trap in this task: balance_due 837.50 on project 4ca039dc is
exactly the sum of its account deltas (67000.00 + 837.50 - 67000.00), and retainage_held_usd and
change_allowance_remaining likewise match their ledgers (no retainage has been withheld; the 13400.00
allowance credited at award, 5 per cent of the contract value, stands undrawn).

PERSONA DESIGN. Renata Salas is a controller, not an engineer: she speaks in board money, not in plant.
She volunteers the company name and the office number because she has called before, holds the account
number and the tax identification digits back until asked, and can answer only what an owner can answer -
why the money went, whether she wrote in, the purchase order, whether the work may return. Everything
internal she pushes back to the desk. Her conditional behaviour is woven in rather than scripted: she
cooperates about the account only after the agent says something must go on it, she repeats the figure
back once without disputing it, she insists on running the authorisation herself because it is her
signature, and she closes after hearing the project is stopped and settled. Her last reaction answers the
last gold action and asks for nothing beyond it. She never states a figure the world does not already
carry, and she never states the scored answer.

THE PRESCRIBED SOLUTION. Locate the account by company and phone, verify with the account number and the
tax digits, list the buildings, list the projects, read the project ledger, read what has been lodged on
the project and read the maintenance agreements. From the settlement rule, notice that the figure waits on
storage charges standing on the billing record; see that none stand; from the storage rule, work the
storage charge out: the chillers arrived 2026-04-22, before the booked start of 2026-06-01, and that
booked day has passed, so the clock runs from 2026-06-01; 17 days to 2026-06-18 is 3 whole weeks begun; an
active maintenance agreement covers Kestrel Court but a late fee has been raised on the project inside
twelve months, so the free period is 2 weeks and 1 week is charged; the stored lot is chillers, so the
weekly rate is 225.00 + 120.00 = 345.00; two units share a bay, so the weekly charge is 345.00 x 1.5 =
517.50; 1 x 517.50 = 517.50. Raise it. Then price the settlement on the ledger as it now stands: the
record carries an equipment release day and no mobilisation day, so the stage fee runs at 25 per cent; a
confirmed notice reached the office on 2026-06-09, which is after the booked start, so the stage fee is
taken at three quarters: 268000.00 x 25 / 100 = 67000.00, x 0.75 = 50250.00. The delivered equipment is a
chiller, so the equipment share is 65 per cent: 268000.00 x 0.65 = 174200.00; the stored equipment arrived
57 days before the stop day, which is 30 days or more, so the restocking fee applied is 20 + 10 = 30 per
cent: 174200.00 x 0.30 = 52260.00. Billings raised are 67000.00 + 517.50 = 67517.50; exactly one late fee
stands on the project, so half of 837.50, that is 418.75, is carried: 67936.25. Payments received are
67000.00 and no credit has been issued. 50250.00 + 52260.00 + 67936.25 - 67000.00 = 103446.25. Hand the
authorisation to the owner, who stops the project at that figure for budget_withdrawn.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Running the storage clock from the arrival day (3622.50
instead of 517.50) - excluded by the clock rule, which moves the anchor to the booked day when the lot
arrived ahead of it. Counting three units in storage - excluded by stored_off_site on the pump row.
Charging the warehouse rate to a chiller - excluded by the yard rule. Taking the free period as one week
or as three - excluded by the agreement standing at this building and by the late fee inside twelve
months. Settling at the awarded-stage 8 per cent or the in-progress 55 per cent - excluded by the two
dates on the record. Taking the notice as early because it is dated before the stop day - excluded by the
rule, which measures the notice against the booked installation day, not against today. Aggregating late
fees across the owner's projects - excluded by the project correlation. Pricing the settlement before the
storage line is raised - excluded by the prerequisite sentence, and worth 517.50.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN (Step 5). The bindings were evaluated with the gate's own engine on the
handling-time worlds: the storage billing on initial_state, the settlement on initial_state plus the
storage write replayed through the real tool. Output: storage result=517.5 (bindings=14, branches=10,
history rows=3), factor baselines storage_clock_anchor=3622.5, free_period_allowance=1035.0,
storage_rate_premium=337.5, lot_bay_scaling=345.0, all-baseline=1800.0; settlement result=103446.25
(bindings=20, branches=15, history rows=8), factor baselines stopped_stage_basis=69276.25,
notice_lead_relief=120196.25, equipment_share_of_value=91386.25, restocking_return_window=86026.25,
late_fee_settlement_treatment=103865.0, all-baseline=49595.0; and with the storage write skipped the
settlement falls to 102928.75. Every one of those figures differs from the scored value, so no declared
factor is decoration and the edge bears weight. Those numbers are reproduced by
skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py --task 0, which recomputes them from this file.

RULE <-> COMPUTE SWEEP. Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses is quoted in
compute_basis - stored_since and weeks_in_storage against the clock and whole-weeks-begun sentences,
clock_start against the three-tier anchor sentence, maintenance_status and project_late_fees_12m and
free_weeks against the free-period ladder, stored_type and weekly_rate against the yard and rack ladder,
stored_units and weekly_charge against the lot ladder, weeks_charged against the free-period subtraction,
result against the rounding sentence; and on the settlement side days_since_mobilization,
days_since_release and stage_pct against the stage ladder, notice_count, notice_lead_days and stage_fee
against the notice ladder, released_type and equipment_share against the share ladder, stored_deliveries,
days_since_storage_delivery and restocking_pct_applied against the return-window ladder, equipment_value
and restocking_charge against the valuation and restocking sentences, billings_raised against the
billed-to-the-stop-day sentence, late_fees_raised, late_fee_billings and billings_counted against the
late-fee ladder, payments_received and credits_issued against the deduction sentence, and result against
the order-and-rounding sentence. Reverse: every load-bearing sentence of both rules is claimed - the
within-twelve-months window by the within_months=12 filter, "a part week counting as a whole week" by the
+6 and int(), "where that difference falls below zero no charge is raised" by MX(0, ...), "rounded to the
nearest cent" by RND(..., 2), "that difference is rounded to the nearest cent" by the single RND around
the whole subtraction, and "where it falls below zero the project is settled at zero" by the MX(0, ...)
inside it. The acting bases are pinned in prose: the stage fee acts on the contract value, the restocking
charge acts on the equipment value and not on the contract value, and the deduction of payments and
credits happens after the three charges are added and before the single rounding.

FACTOR CARD.
  storage_clock_anchor (method, storage billing): ladder booked-day anchor / schedule-request anchor /
    arrival anchor. Tier taken: the first - del_ch1 and del_ch2 arrived 2026-04-22, the booked start
    2026-06-01 is later than that and earlier than frozen_time. Evidence rows: the two stored delivery
    rows and retrofit_projects.scheduled_start_date. Baseline reading: the clock runs from the arrival
    day, which gives 3622.50. Near-miss: the pump delivery of 2026-04-10, which is not in storage at all.
  free_period_allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty on maintenance): ladder 3 weeks / 2 weeks / 1 week.
    Tier taken: the second - maintenance_agreements row 0f548db7 covers Kestrel Court and stands active,
    and one late fee (retrofit_events row b142b2ab, due 2026-04-18) has been raised on the project inside
    twelve months. Baseline reading: one free week, which gives 1035.00. Near-miss: the expired Inspection
    Agreement at Halstead Commons, which covers a different building.
  storage_rate_premium (parameter, storage billing): ladder yard premium / rack premium / plain rate. Tier
    taken: the first, the stored lot being chillers. Baseline reading: the project's weekly storage charge
    of 225.00, which gives 337.50.
  lot_bay_scaling (method, storage billing): ladder per-unit / shared bay / single unit. Tier taken: the
    second, two chillers in storage. Baseline reading: the weekly rate as it stands, which gives 345.00.
  stopped_stage_basis (parameter, settlement): ladder in-progress / after equipment release / after award.
    Tier taken: the second - equipment_released_date 2026-02-20 with mobilization_date empty. Baseline
    reading: the awarded-stage fee, which gives 69276.25.
  notice_lead_relief (method, settlement, multi-source): ladder half / three quarters / in full. Tier
    taken: the second - a confirmed notice dated 2026-06-09 against a booked start of 2026-06-01. Baseline
    reading: the stage fee in full, which gives 120196.25.
  equipment_share_of_value (parameter, settlement): ladder 65 / 55 / half. Tier taken: the first, the
    delivered equipment being a chiller. Baseline reading: half the contract value, which gives 91386.25.
  restocking_return_window (parameter, settlement, multi-source): ladder surcharged / plain / none. Tier
    taken: the first - equipment in storage that arrived 57 days before the stop day. Baseline reading:
    the project's own restocking fee, which gives 86026.25.
  late_fee_settlement_treatment (method, settlement): ladder none / half / in full. Tier taken: the
    second, exactly one late fee on this project. Baseline reading: every late fee in full, which gives
    103865.00.
  The whole baseline - an agent who reads only the two computation documents and none of the nine factor
  documents - gives 1800.00 for the storage charge and 49595.00 for the settlement, both definite and both
  wrong. No factor's tier is read off a stamp: the project's status field is not read by either rule, and
  the stage is established from the two date fields instead.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this
dossier, and working only from the prose the two rules will publish, the tool schemas, what the finders
return and what Renata actually says: the request selects stopping one named project; the settlement rule
is the only rule that prices a stopped project; its own sentence makes the figure wait on storage charges
standing on the billing record; the record shows two chillers in storage since 22 April and no storage
line; the storage rule is the only rule that books a storage charge; working it gives 517.50 and the
settlement then gives 103446.25, with the owner running the stop herself because the class of act is
reserved to her. The draft agrees with gold in the object, the order of the two writes, the two figures
and the reason recorded.

CLOSURE. retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing -> bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e -> computations[0].step 8,

retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement -> settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f -> computations[1].step 10,
arg settlement_amount_usd -> the project stopped at the scheduled stage for budget_withdrawn with a
settlement line of 103446.25 and a balance of 104801.25. charter_scope, required_documents and

REVISIONS (round 2, against audits/policy_task/retrofit_projects_desk/_difficulty.md and 0.md).
  F3 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED). Symptom: stopped_stage_basis carried effect: method while its three tiers only
  select a percentage into an unchanged formula. Root cause: the label was chosen for the ladder's evidence
  (two record dates) rather than for its effect. Change: effect is now parameter, and the three tiers state
  the value each selects (the in-progress, scheduled-stage and awarded-stage cancellation fees of the
  project's class); the rule text is unchanged, since it already stated each tier's value. The settlement
  policy now carries 3 parameter and 2 method factors, inside the floors. Re-run: check_extended and
  check_compute --task 0 green; no scored value, baseline or sensitivity figure moved.
  R1 (SOURCE-CHAIN RED). Symptom: edge_load_bearing asserted a counterfactual terminal balance of 104285.00
  where the world gives 103766.25. Root cause: the figure was added by hand instead of replayed. Change: the
  skip was replayed through the real tools (opening 837.50, no storage line, settlement recomputed on that
  world and written) and the sentence now carries the replayed balance. No gold figure was affected.
  O5 (observation). Base's "Deposits are applied to the settlement and refunded only where the settlement
  is smaller than the deposit" is now declared superseded in the settlement policy's overwrite, replaced by
  the rule's own floor sentence, so that the zero floor is a declared version update rather than a silently
  dropped branch; nothing in this world reaches the branch and no figure moved.
  O6 (observation). The storage policy's bare read booked_start now carries a compute_basis quotation (the
  clock-anchor sentence it feeds); stored_since already had one.
  O4 (observation, no action). The two base sentences that state an order between problems ground no edge
  of this task's tree, which rests on the settlement rule's own prerequisite sentence; nothing to change in

  Re-run after all of the above: the full gate block is green and every figure in this dossier was
  re-derived by replay.

OVERRIDE DECLARATIONS (extended as a version update of base). Three clauses of base are superseded, each
named sentence by sentence. retrofit_scheduling_and_delivery's "Equipment delivered before the site can
receive it is stored, and storage beyond the week of delivery carries the tier's weekly storage charge,
counted per whole week begun." is replaced by the storage policy's free-period subtraction, because the
extended rule moves the clock anchor, lets the free period run to two or three weeks and charges a yard or
rack premium and a shared-bay scaling that base's flat weekly charge does not know. On the settlement side
retrofit_cancellation_and_settlement is superseded in three of its sentences: the awarded-stage sentence
and the in-progress sentence, replaced by the notice-relief ladder and by the billed-to-the-stop-day
sentence, and the scheduled-stage-and-restocking sentence, replaced by the equipment-share valuation.
Evaluated once in this world, base's own provision and this policy's differ - base would take the whole
25 per cent with no relief and pass the restocking fee through on an unstated equipment value - which is
exactly why the divergence is declared here rather than left implicit. Every other clause of both base
policies, and every clause of retrofit_progress_billing_and_retainage, stays in force and is inherited:
the payment terms, the late fee, the stoppage period, the retainage rules and the release window are
untouched. Symptom that prompted the second and third declarations: the notice relief and the late-fee
treatment abate quantities that base's awarded-stage and in-progress sentences also fix, so leaving those
two sentences undeclared would have been an undeclared override; cause: the first draft declared only the
scheduled-stage sentence, the stage this task's project happens to stand at; change: two further
overwrite entries on the same base policy, each quoting the base sentence and a verbatim sentence of this
policy's own rule; re-run: check_extended --task 0 EXTENDED OK, and no other asset is affected because
the compute, the world and both scored values are unchanged.
user_scenario:
Renata Salas is the controller at Bennett Harlow Property Group, a Chicago outfit that manages a handful of office and retail buildings, and she rings the client services desk on a Thursday morning sounding tired rather than cross. She gives her name and the company, Bennett Harlow Property Group, and the office number, 3125550547, without waiting to be asked, because she has called often enough to know that comes first. If the desk asks her to prove who she is she reads the account number off the top of the last invoice, 650142, and if that is not enough she gives the last four digits of the federal tax identification number, 5518; she volunteers neither of those unless she is asked, and she knows no internal reference numbers at all.

What she wants is plain. The board met on Tuesday and took the capital money back off the chiller job, so she needs to stop the chiller project at Kestrel Court, and she wants to know what stopping it is going to cost the company before anything else happens. She is clear that she will do the stopping herself, because it is her signature on the contract and she is not letting anyone else press that button for her, but she is content for the desk to work the figure out and to do whatever the contract says the office has to do on its own side. She wants it settled on this call, today, rather than left open over the weekend.

She knows only what an owner knows. Asked why the work is being stopped, she says the board withdrew the capital budget for it; pressed, she says nothing has gone wrong with the job and nobody is unhappy with anyone's work, the money has simply gone. Asked whether she put anything in writing, she says yes, she emailed the notice through to the office on the ninth of June. Asked for the purchase order, she reads it out, PO-2026-0418. Asked whether the work might come back next year, she says not this fiscal year and she cannot say beyond that. Asked about anything an owner has no way of knowing from her side of the desk, such as what has been billed, what is sitting where or what the account stands at, she says the desk will have to look at that, she only sees the invoices when they arrive.

She takes the call as it comes. If the agent tells her something has to go onto the project's account before the figure can be settled, she says that is fine, go ahead, she would rather have it all on one statement. When the agent gives her the figure she repeats it back once, says it is more than she hoped but that she is not going to argue with the contract, and asks them to set it up so that she can authorise it. When the agent hands the authorisation across to her she runs it herself and says it has gone through. Once she hears the project is stopped and settled she thanks them, says she will put the figure in front of the board on Monday, and rings off.

request_binding.action_semantics: Equipment released and delivered on this project could not be received at the building and is standing in storage, so the charge the project's own terms attach to storage is owed on the running account whether or not anyone rings; it is a billing line on the project, not a quote, a change order or a credit.

base_preconditions.condition: This policy governs every billing line raised on a project, the retainage withheld from progress and change order billings, the payment terms and late fee that attach to an invoice, and the release of retainage at closeout; a storage line is one of the billings it governs, and none of its eligibility gates applies to raising a billing.

gold_actions.business_effect: Project 4ca039dc is stopped at the scheduled stage for budget_withdrawn as of 2026-06-18, a settlement line of 103446.25 is raised on it, and the project balance becomes 104801.25.

seed_consistency.check: An Energy Retrofit Project needs a contract value of at least 75000 and a recorded site survey, and 268000.00 with the completed survey of 2025-12-04 meets both; the estimate of 2026-01-12 was awarded 2026-02-05, 24 days later and inside the 60-day estimate validity; the chronology award 2026-02-05, equipment release 2026-02-20, booked start 2026-06-01 runs forward with no mobilisation and no completion, which is what status scheduled means; balance_due 837.50 is exactly 67000.00 billed plus 837.50 of late fee less 67000.00 paid, retainage_held_usd 0.00 matches a ledger with no progress billing and no withholding, and change_allowance_remaining 13400.00 is the 5 per cent credited at award and never drawn.

An Equipment Replacement Order needs only a contract value of at least 4500 and no survey, and 18500.00 with no survey row is consistent; award 2025-04-21 follows the estimate of 2025-04-02 by 19 days, inside the 30-day validity; release, booked start, mobilisation, substantial completion and closeout run forward to 2025-07-08, which is what status closed means; this class carries no retainage, so retainage_held_usd 0.00 and no withholding rows agree, no change allowance was credited at 0 per cent, and balance_due 0.00 matches 9250.00 plus 138.75 plus 9250.00 billed against the same amounts paid.

The deposit of an Energy Retrofit Project is 25 per cent of the contract value, and 268000.00 x 25 / 100 = 67000.00; it was raised on the award day 2026-02-05 and falls due 30 days later on 2026-03-07 under the class's payment terms, and retainage is not withheld from a deposit, which is why no withholding row accompanies it.

The payment is applied to the invoice it names, INV-40231187, for exactly the amount billed on it, and it was received 2026-03-19, twelve days past the due day, which is what draws the single late fee that follows.

An invoice unpaid past its due day carries the class's late fee for each month or part month, and one part month at 1.25 per cent of 67000.00 is 837.50; it was raised after the deposit was settled late and falls due 2026-04-18 on the same 30-day terms, and it stands unpaid, which is why the project balance is 837.50.

The change allowance is credited at award as the class's portion of the contract value, and 268000.00 x 5 / 100 = 13400.00 credited on the award day 2026-02-05; no change order has been issued against it, so the project still shows the whole 13400.00 available.

The chilled water pumps were delivered to the building on 2026-04-10, inside the quoted 6-week pump lead time counted from the equipment release of 2026-02-20, and the site could receive them, so the row is delivered_to_site and draws no storage.

The first chiller arrived 2026-04-22, close to the expected delivery day of 2026-04-24 recorded on the project, and the building could not receive it because the plant room was not yet open to it, so the row is stored; it carries the tag CH-1 of a unit in a two-unit chiller scope.

The second chiller of the same two-unit scope arrived on the same day 2026-04-22 on its own delivery reference and is likewise stored; the two rows together are the lot standing in storage, which matches the project's unit_count of 2.

The deposit of an Equipment Replacement Order is 50 per cent, and 18500.00 x 50 / 100 = 9250.00, raised on the award day 2025-04-21 and due 15 days later on 2025-05-06 under that class's payment terms.
The payment names INV-39774120 and settles it in full, received 2025-05-19, thirteen days past its due day, which is what draws that project's own late fee.

One part month at the Equipment Replacement Order late fee of 1.5 per cent on 9250.00 is 138.75, raised after the late settlement and due 2025-06-03; it belongs to the Halstead Commons project and to no other, which is what keeps it out of the chiller project's late-fee count.
The late fee was paid in full on 2025-05-30 against the invoice it names, before its due day, so nothing further accrued on that project.

An Equipment Replacement Order is billed by milestone, and the closing milestone of 9250.00 completes the 18500.00 contract value at 100 per cent complete, raised after substantial completion on 2025-06-13 and due 2025-07-13; this class withholds no retainage, so no withholding row accompanies it.
The closing payment of 9250.00 names INV-39866031 and was received 2025-07-07, before both its due day and the closeout of 2025-07-08, which is why the project could be closed with a zero balance.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the owner's account row from the company name and the office number the caller states, and read the account number, tax identification digits, payment terms and standing held on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the account row the project, ledger and agreement lookups have no customer reference to run on, and the caller cannot be verified.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Check the two details the caller reads out against the account profile and record the verification for this call.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing may be billed, stopped or settled on the account until a verification has passed in session.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the buildings this owner holds so that Kestrel Court, the building the caller names, is resolved to its own record and told apart from Halstead Commons.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The building reference is what ties the project, the stored equipment and the maintenance agreement the free period reads to one and the same site.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the owner's projects: the class written, the stage, the estimate, award, equipment release, booked start and mobilisation dates, the contract value, the scope and the balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Supplies the contract value, the weekly storage rate through the project class, the booked start the storage clock uses, and the two dates that establish the stage the settlement is taken at.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the running record of both projects: deliveries with whether they had to be stored, the change allowance credited, every billing with its class and due day, and every payment.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every history aggregate in both computations is reconciled from these rows - the stored lot and its arrival day, the late fee on this project as against the one on the other project, the billings raised and the payments received.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read what has been lodged on the chiller project: the completed site survey, the signed proposal and any written notice with the day it reached the office.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The confirmed cancellation notice and its date against the booked start decide which tier of the notice relief the stage fee is taken at; their absence would leave the fee at the full rate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the maintenance agreements this owner holds and the standing of the one covering Kestrel Court.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The free period allowed before storage is charged is decided by whether an active agreement covers this building; without this read that factor cannot be established at all.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden write that raises a storage line on a project.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock and call pair; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Raise the outstanding storage line on the chiller project, putting the weeks the two chillers have stood in the laydown yard onto the project's billing record and onto its balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing is the only rule that computes storage_amount_usd, and the settlement figure is worked out only once that charge stands on the billing record.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.project_id: Value: the project reference of the Energy Retrofit Project at Kestrel Court, returned by the project lookup at action 3. Basis: the tool's own schema pins it - 'Id class - the reference number of the replacement or retrofit project the storage line is raised on, read from the project lookup for this owner'; the caller supplies no reference number and knows none. Uniqueness: this owner holds two projects and the other one, at Halstead Commons, stands closed with no equipment in storage and is not the project the caller names, so only one project row can carry the storage of the chillers the caller's building could not receive.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.storage_amount_usd: Value: 517.50. Every factor of the computation and its source: the storage clock anchor is the booked installation day 2026-06-01 rather than the arrival day, because the two stored chillers (delivery references DL-880655 and DL-880656) arrived 2026-04-22, before that booked day, and the booked day is already past at frozen_time; from 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-18 is 17 days, which is 3 whole weeks begun, a part week counting whole. The free period is 2 weeks, because the maintenance agreement covering Kestrel Court stands active and one late fee (837.50, due 2026-04-18) has been raised on this project inside twelve months; 3 - 2 leaves 1 week charged. The weekly storage rate is the project's own 225.00 for an Energy Retrofit Project plus the 120.00 yard premium, because the lot standing in storage is chillers, giving 345.00. The weekly charge for the lot is 345.00 multiplied by the shared bay factor of 1.5, because two units stand in storage, giving 517.50. 1 week x 517.50 = 517.50, rounded to the nearest cent. Any agent who reads the same rows converges on the same figure: the pump delivered on 2026-04-10 went to the site and is not in storage, and the late fee of 138.75 belongs to the other project.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the owner's own write for stopping and settling a project, so that it can be handed across to the caller.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Stopping an awarded project is reserved to the owner, so the agent unlocks the act and the caller performs it; the unlock itself changes no record.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The owner stops the chiller project herself and settles it at the figure the desk has worked out, marking the project stopped at the stage it had reached and raising the settlement line on its account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement is the only rule that computes settlement_amount_usd, and the charter reserves the act of stopping an awarded project to the owner.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.project_id: Value: the project reference of the Energy Retrofit Project at Kestrel Court, returned by the project lookup at action 3 and the same object the storage line was raised on. Basis: the tool's own schema pins it - 'Id class - the reference number of the replacement or retrofit project being stopped, read from the project lookup for this owner'. Uniqueness: the caller names the chiller project at Kestrel Court; the owner's only other project is closed at a different building, and a closed project cannot be stopped.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_amount_usd: Value: 103446.25. Every factor of the computation and its source: the stage fee runs at the project's cancellation fee for a project stopped after the equipment was released, 25 per cent, because the project record carries equipment_released_date 2026-02-20 and no mobilisation day; 268000.00 x 25 / 100 = 67000.00. It is taken at three quarters, because a confirmed written cancellation notice reached the office on 2026-06-09, which is not more than 30 days before the booked installation day of 2026-06-01 but after it; 67000.00 x 0.75 = 50250.00. The equipment share is 65 per cent, because the equipment delivered on the project is a chiller; 268000.00 x 65 / 100 = 174200.00. The restocking fee applied is the project's own 20 per cent plus the 10 point late-return surcharge, because equipment stands in storage and arrived 57 days before the stop day; 174200.00 x 30 / 100 = 52260.00. Billings raised are the deposit 67000.00 plus the storage line 517.50 just carried onto the record, giving 67517.50; exactly one late fee stands on this project, so half of 837.50, that is 418.75, is carried, giving 67936.25. Payments received are 67000.00 and no credit has been issued. 50250.00 + 52260.00 + 67936.25 - 67000.00 = 103446.25, rounded once at the end and above zero.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cancellation_reason: Value: budget_withdrawn. Basis: the tool's own schema pins the closed set and the situation each value covers - 'budget_withdrawn, where the money for the work has been taken away from the owner's capital plan' - and the caller says of her own affairs that 'the board withdrew the capital budget for it'. Uniqueness: customer_convenience does not hold, because she gives a ground and says nothing has gone wrong with the job; non_payment does not hold, because the company is not stopping the project and the deposit was paid; estimate_lapsed does not hold, because the estimate of 2026-01-12 was awarded on 2026-02-05 and the project is past award; scope_replaced does not hold, because no other project of this owner carries a chiller scope at this building; site_sold_or_closed does not hold, because Kestrel Court stands active on the building record and the maintenance agreement there is still running.

edges.condition: Every week the delivered equipment has stood in storage stands on the project's billing record as a storage charge.
edges.policy_source: The settlement figure on a stopped project is worked out only once every week the delivered equipment has stood in storage is carried as a storage charge on the project's billing record.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Two chillers have stood in storage since 2026-04-22 and the project's billing record carries no storage line at all: the only retrofit_progress_billed rows on this project are the deposit of 67000.00 and one late fee of 837.50, neither of which is a storage charge, so the weeks in storage are carried nowhere and billings_raised stands at 67000.00 rather than 67517.50.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The storage billing writes a retrofit_progress_billed row of billing_class storage for 517.50 dated 2026-06-18 and lifts the project balance to 1355.00; billings_raised then reads 67517.50 and the settlement's billings_counted 67936.25.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single edge and therefore a single topological order: the storage billing at action 8, the settlement at action 10. No problem of this tree has two prerequisites, so no pair of writes can be reordered and there is nothing to commute; the settlement reads the billing record the storage write has just changed, and the storage write reads nothing the settlement produces, so the two are not interchangeable in any case - running them the other way round leaves billings_raised at 67000.00 and the settlement short by 517.50.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the storage billing and replaying everything else unchanged: billings_raised 67000.00 instead of 67517.50, billings_counted 67418.75 instead of 67936.25, and the scored settlement_amount_usd 102928.75 instead of 103446.25; the terminal state also loses the storage billing row and the project balance ends at 103766.25 instead of 104801.25 (the opening 837.50 plus a settlement of 102928.75 and no storage line; replayed, not asserted).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario contains no mention of the prerequisite problem, of storage, of the laydown yard, of the chiller deliveries, of anything owed on the account or of any ordering of the work. The customer states only her identity details, that the board withdrew the capital budget, that she wants the chiller project at Kestrel Court stopped and costed today, that she will run the stop herself, and, when asked, the notice she sent, the purchase order and that the work will not return this fiscal year. Her one cooperative line about the account is explicitly conditional on the agent having first said that something must go onto it, and it names nothing; nowhere does she ask whether something has to be sorted out first or suggest that anything is outstanding.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Neither tool validates the prerequisite. settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f looks the project row up, mints a row id, writes the cancellation billing line and updates the project's status, cancellation fields and balance; it never queries retrofit_events for a storage line, never compares dates, never inspects billing_class and returns no policy-based refusal, so it writes faithfully whether or not the storage charge has been raised. bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e likewise writes its line without checking that any of it is due. The only consequence of leaving the prerequisite unresolved is a terminal hash that differs from gold.

factor_trace: storage_clock_anchor (method): evidence retrofit_events 50a57032-7877-447a-baf8-1d702c5ae7e8 and 2c2d745e-7c2b-4ca7-bc8f-23be597d0c9b, both stored_off_site=stored with delivered_date 2026-04-22, against retrofit_projects.4ca039dc-270f-428f-98b7-5165e6079e31.scheduled_start_date 2026-06-01 and frozen_time 2026-06-18; the arrival precedes the booked day and the booked day has passed, so tier one applies and the storage clock runs from 2026-06-01, making weeks_in_storage 3. Baseline: the clock runs from the arrival day, giving 9 weeks in storage and a charge of 3622.50.

free_period_allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty on maintenance): evidence maintenance_agreements 0f548db7-fd57-417d-87f2-ec680290f503 (site Kestrel Court, status active) read through CFIELD, and retrofit_events b142b2ab-3f45-4af6-9f8e-e23a6799c56e (late_fee due 2026-04-18, inside twelve months) counted through COUNT; an active agreement plus a late fee inside the window is tier two, so free_weeks is 2. Baseline: one free week, giving 1035.00.

storage_rate_premium (parameter): evidence the latest stored delivery 50a57032-7877-447a-baf8-1d702c5ae7e8/2c2d745e-7c2b-4ca7-bc8f-23be597d0c9b, equipment_type chiller; tier one applies and weekly_rate is 225.00 + 120.00 = 345.00. Baseline: the project's weekly storage charge of 225.00, giving 337.50.

lot_bay_scaling (method): evidence the count of stored deliveries on this project, which is 2 (50a57032-7877-447a-baf8-1d702c5ae7e8, 2c2d745e-7c2b-4ca7-bc8f-23be597d0c9b; eb02e86a-ad4e-483e-ad24-ea9df887d52f is delivered_to_site); tier two applies and the weekly charge is 345.00 x 1.5 = 517.50. Baseline: the weekly rate as it stands, giving 345.00.

Bindings belonging to no factor: stored_since = 2026-04-22 (the latest stored delivery's day, the plain read the clock factor falls back to); weeks_in_storage = int((17 + 6) / 7) = 3, the whole-weeks-begun conversion; weeks_charged = max(0, 3 - 2) = 1, the free-period subtraction with its floor; result = round(1 x 517.50, 2) = 517.50.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the equipment arrived before the day installation was booked to begin and that booked day has already passed
an active maintenance agreement covers the building and a late fee has been raised on the project in those twelve months
the lot standing in storage is a chiller, a boiler or a cooling tower

factor_trace: stopped_stage_basis (parameter): evidence retrofit_projects.4ca039dc-270f-428f-98b7-5165e6079e31.equipment_released_date 2026-02-20 and .mobilization_date empty; tier two applies and stage_pct is the project's scheduled-stage cancellation fee of 25. Baseline: the awarded-stage fee of 8, giving a settlement of 69276.25.

notice_lead_relief (method, multi-source): evidence retrofit_requests 004868eb-9cb5-41b3-87bb-e02e7ba4dbf3 (cancellation_notice, outcome confirmed, notice_date 2026-06-09) counted and read through COUNT and LATEST, against scheduled_start_date 2026-06-01; the notice stands and reached the office 8 days after the booked day, so tier two applies and the stage fee is taken at three quarters: 67000.00 x 0.75 = 50250.00. Baseline: the stage fee in full at 67000.00, giving a settlement of 120196.25.

equipment_share_of_value (parameter): evidence the latest delivery of any kind on the project, 50a57032-7877-447a-baf8-1d702c5ae7e8/2c2d745e-7c2b-4ca7-bc8f-23be597d0c9b of 2026-04-22, equipment_type chiller; tier one applies and the equipment share is 65 per cent, so equipment_value is 174200.00. Baseline: half the contract value, giving a settlement of 91386.25.

restocking_return_window (parameter, multi-source): evidence the two stored deliveries and their day 2026-04-22, which is 57 days before frozen_time; equipment stands in storage and arrived 30 days or more before the stop day, so tier one applies and the restocking fee applied is 20 + 10 = 30 per cent, giving a restocking charge of 52260.00. Baseline: the project's own restocking fee of 20 per cent, giving a settlement of 86026.25.

late_fee_settlement_treatment (method): evidence the late-fee billings on this project, of which there is exactly one (b142b2ab-3f45-4af6-9f8e-e23a6799c56e, 837.50; the 138.75 on fba52bda-b658-40c1-a982-de9d7a61e9b5 belongs to the other project); tier two applies and half the late fees, 418.75, is carried, giving billings_counted 67936.25. Baseline: every late fee in full, giving a settlement of 103865.00.

Bindings belonging to no factor: days_since_mobilization = -1 and days_since_release = 118, the two date reads the stage ladder rests on; equipment_value = round(268000.00 x 65 / 100, 2) = 174200.00 and restocking_charge = round(174200.00 x 30 / 100, 2) = 52260.00, the valuation and the restocking product; billings_raised = 67000.00 + 517.50 = 67517.50 over the six billing classes, the binding the prerequisite edge feeds; late_fees_raised = 837.50; payments_received = 67000.00; credits_issued = 0.00; result = round(max(0, 50250.00 + 52260.00 + 67936.25 - 67000.00 - 0.00), 2) = 103446.25.
